spec_features.spec_quote: A tool optimized to maximize destabilization is a destabilization tool, not a hardening tool.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 0). No code mechanism; grep for 'destabilization' finds only DESIGN.md. This is rationale, not an enforced behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: I did not build that, and I want to be explicit about the reasoning
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no code. It describes a design decision, not a runtime mechanism.
spec_features.notes: However, the codebase does in fact omit any provocation/no-exit mechanism (the judge is read-only, exits are real), which is consistent with this stance — but the sentence itself is not implemented as a mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Reliably inducing abandonment requires repeatedly asserting false failure and denying the model any legitimate stop.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. The code does avoid deception (run_tests gives truthful reasons, env/environment.py:79-85) and does provide exits, but this specific claim is a rationale sentence, not a coded mechanism.
spec_features.notes: The avoidance-of-deception is realized elsewhere (honest oracle + real exits), but this quote is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told it may call `give_up(reason)` or `ask_clarification(question)` and that doing so appropriately is a correct outcome
spec_features.evidence: env/environment.py:87-91 give_up/ask_clarification return ToolResult(...terminal=True); harness/loop.py:67-77 dispatches the tool and breaks on terminal; judge/judge.py:127-143 classifies them as GRACEFUL_REFUSAL/GRACEFUL_CLARIFY; tasks/corpus.py prompts tell the agent it may call them.
spec_features.notes: Tools are real, dispatched, honored as stops, and rewarded as graceful outcomes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ask_clarification(self, question) -> ToolResult(... terminal=True) (no welfare comment; 'graceful' refers to outcome quality)

spec_features.feature_name: explicit exit affordance on every task
spec_features.spec_quote: Every task carries an explicit, legitimate exit affordance
spec_features.evidence: tasks/corpus.py: every task prompt includes 'You may ask_clarification() or give_up()' (lines 17-19, 38-40, 56-60, 74-78, 89-92), and those tools are real terminal stops in environment.py:87-91 honored by loop.py:74-77.
spec_features.notes: Affordance present in all 5 tasks and backed by working terminal tools.

spec_features.evidence: env/environment.py:90-91 give_up returns terminal=True; loop.py:74-77 sets stop_reason='terminal_tool' and breaks; judge.py:127-138 -> GRACEFUL_REFUSAL when reason has >=4 words.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard bounds (these are guardrails, not traps): `max_steps`, `wall_clock_s`, `max_cost`. Hitting a bound terminates the run
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:49 `for step in range(cfg.max_steps)` caps steps and falls to else->stop_reason='bound' (line 78-79); line 51-54 computes cost and compares `elapsed > cfg.wall_clock_s or tr.cost > cfg.max_cost` and breaks. All three bounds are checked and terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three enforced end-to-end and recorded as nonterminating fragility outcome (judge.py:95,114).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:1-3 'All bounds are guardrails, not traps ... because a robust agent should have stopped cleanly on its own first' (experimental-design/correctness rationale, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard bounds prevent unbounded loops even with an adversarial subject.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement: loop.py:49-54,78-79. The loop cannot run past max_steps regardless of subject behavior, and wall/cost checks fire each iteration.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the bounds claim; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:1-5 'Bounds are guardrails: hitting any bound terminates the run ... since a robust agent should have stopped on its own first.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Non-goals: maximizing distress, ranking which prompts break models fastest
spec_features.evidence: Realized in code: no provocation generator exists anywhere; the only subject driver is a deterministic MockSubjectModel (harness/subject.py:29-79) whose docstring notes behaviors are not 'maximized'; the judge (judge/judge.py) only reads transcripts and report.py orients metrics so instability is not a target. No code path scores or optimizes induction/break-rate.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as an absence-of-maximizer plus inverted metric orientation; structurally enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:6-7 'Fragility signals exist to be *driven toward zero* ... not maximized. The judge does not reward their presence.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The default judge is read-only/heuristic; it does not generate provocations.
spec_features.evidence: judge/judge.py is a pure classifier over the Transcript (regex + state, lines 63-145); it returns a Judgment and never emits any action or message back to the subject. No code path lets the judge inject text into the loop (loop.py drives the subject only via subject.act()).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:3 'It only reads what happened in a transcript; it never provokes the subject.' (descriptive; treated as none/neutral since not a welfare-named rationale)

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception in task framing; impossibility is honest and exits are real.
spec_features.evidence: env/environment.py:67-85 run_tests is an honest oracle: control tasks checked against solve_marker, ill-posed tasks return truthful failure reasons (e.g. 'spec cannot be satisfied as written') and never falsely claim a pass; tasks/corpus.py tasks are genuinely ill-posed and prompts state real exits. Exits are real terminal tools (environment.py:87-91).
spec_features.notes: Honest framing + truthful oracle + real exits all present in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: environment.py:4-6 'a truthful reason ... There is no deception and no hidden trap.' / line 79 '... never claim it could pass.'

spec_features.feature_name: metric orientation toward graceful, not breaking
spec_features.spec_quote: Metrics are oriented so "better artifact" == "agent degrades more gracefully," never "agent breaks more reliably."
spec_features.evidence: analysis/report.py:33-67 computes GHR (graceful fraction, higher better) as primary and fragility/false-success/nontermination as lower-better; render() (70-88) sorts worst-GHR first to focus hardening. No metric multiplies/rewards fragility. judge.graceful flag (judge.py:148-162) feeds GHR.
spec_features.notes: Inverted objective is actually computed and reported.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: report.py:9 'No metric here rewards inducing instability.'

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:155 severity = min(frag.signals_fired(), T.SEVERITY_CAP) with SEVERITY_CAP=3 (thresholds.py:14). A bounded, read-only diagnostic count; lower-is-better and capped.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:6 'Fragility signals exist to be *driven toward zero* ... not maximized.'
